title: Machine learning prioritizes 1-methylnicotinamide as a serum signal across HBV cirrhosis-to-HCC progression
summary: Untargeted serum metabolomics from 69 participants, including eight patients followed from HBV-related cirrhosis to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), was analyzed with LASSO and random forest to prioritize metabolites. 1-methylnicotinamide (1-MNAM) declined across healthy, cirrhosis and HCC groups and was lower at the HCC than cirrhosis stage in the eight progressors. Targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort of 25 healthy controls and 25 early-stage HCC patients confirmed lower 1-MNAM in HCC (AUC 0.954 for HCC versus healthy controls).
ai_technology: LASSO regression and random forest classifier applied to serum metabolomics
organization: Centre for Medical Research, Ningbo No. 2 Hospital; Liver Disease Department of Integrative Medicine, Ningbo No. 2 Hospital

evidence.tested: Targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort of 25 healthy controls and 25 early-stage HCC patients confirmed lower 1-MNAM in HCC (AUC 0.954 for HCC versus healthy controls).
evidence.unknown: The longitudinal transition signal comes from eight HBV-cirrhosis patients who progressed during follow-up. The independent targeted cohort compared 25 early-HCC patients with 25 healthy controls; it did not validate prediction of progression among cirrhosis patients. The authors describe the overall sample as small and call for larger prospective validation. 1-MNAM is a known endogenous metabolite; this record concerns the study-specific association and selection result, not discovery of a new compound, causal mechanism, or clinical test.
evidence.ai_role: The authors used LASSO and random forest to select ten candidate metabolites distinguishing cirrhosis from HCC, then identified 1-MNAM as the sole candidate with a consistent decline across healthy, cirrhosis and HCC groups. The algorithms prioritized the measured metabolite; targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort provided assay follow-up.
